question: A train leaves Station A at 6:00 AM and travels towards Station B at a constant speed of 60 km/h. Another train leaves Station B at 8:00 AM and travels towards Station A at a constant speed of 90 km/h. The distance between the two stations is 540 km. At what time will the two trains meet?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by the first train in 2 hours (6:00 AM to 8:00 AM) = 60 × 2 = 120 km.

Remaining distance at 8:00 AM = 540 − 120 = 420 km.

Relative speed of both trains moving towards each other = 60 + 90 = 150 km/h.

Time taken to meet after 8:00 AM = 420 ÷ 150 = 2.8 hours = 2 hours 48 minutes.

Meeting time = 8:00 AM + 2 hours 48 minutes = 10:48 AM.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:48 AM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between Station A and Station B = 540 km

Speed of Train 1 (from Station A) = 60 km/h

Speed of Train 2 (from Station B) = 90 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Train 1 starts at 6:00 AM and Train 2 starts at 8:00 AM. Hence, Train 1 travels alone for 2 hours.

⇒ Distance covered by Train 1 in 2 hours = 60 × 2 = 120 km.

⇒ Remaining distance between the two trains at 8:00 AM = 540 − 120 = 420 km.

⇒ At 8:00 AM, both trains are moving towards each other.

⇒ Relative Speed = Speed of Train 1 + Speed of Train 2

⇒ Relative Speed = 60 + 90 = 150 km/h.

⇒ Time required to meet = Remaining distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time = 420 ÷ 150 = 14 ÷ 5 hours.

⇒ Converting hours into hours and minutes: (14 ÷ 5) hours = 2 hours and (4 ÷ 5) × 60 minutes.

⇒ Time taken to meet = 2 hours 48 minutes after 8:00 AM.

⇒ Meeting Time = 8:00 AM + 2 hours 48 minutes = 10:48 AM.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:48 AM.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the absolute difference of their individual speeds: SR = |S₁ − S₂|.

Average Speed

If an object covers equal consecutive distances at speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed over the entire journey is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).
